name: capell-app/wordpress-importer
description: Brings posts, pages and images from a WordPress export file onto a site built with Capell, each one becoming an ordinary page.

healthChecks.label: WordPress Importer WXR reader registration and XML parser dependencies are available to Migration Assistant.

marketplace.summary: Move posts, pages and images from a WordPress export file onto your new site, with a preview that writes nothing first.
marketplace.description: Move a WordPress site's posts and pages into Capell from the export file WordPress gives you. A preview first shows what would be created, skipped or rejected, and writes nothing. Images are fetched from public addresses and files over 50 MB are refused. Comments, users, revisions and custom post types are not brought across. A developer or agency needs to run it from the command line.
marketplace.problem: Moving a long-running WordPress site by hand loses images and leaves old links pointing nowhere.
marketplace.outcome: Posts, pages and images arrive as ordinary pages on the new site, with a preview first and old addresses redirected where possible.

faq.question: What does the import need, and who runs it?
faq.answer: A WordPress export file. An agency or developer runs the import from the command line.

faq.question: Can I see what will happen before anything is written?
faq.answer: Yes. The preview writes nothing and counts what would be created, skipped or rejected.

faq.question: What does not come across from WordPress?
faq.answer: Comments, users, revisions and custom post types stay behind. Shortcodes are taken out, and any text a shortcode wraps is kept as plain text, so a gallery or form shortcode leaves nothing. A post keeps its original date only if WordPress had it published, and everything else arrives unpublished.

faq.question: Will my old WordPress links redirect to the new pages?
faq.answer: They can. With Redirects installed too, each post's old address leads to its new page, and any post that cannot be given one is listed with the reason.

faq.question: What if I run the same export twice?
faq.answer: Posts already imported anywhere on the site are skipped, so a repeat run creates no copies. If an image download fails, retrying picks up where it stopped.
